thread.title: Here are the Bay Area’s highest-paid CEOs in finance

author: Mark Calvey
title: Here are the Bay Area’s highest-paid CEOs in finance
text: – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Aug 27, 2018, 2:48pm PDT The Bay Area’s fintech startups may capture the glamour, but it's the more established finance players that can afford to pay big bucks to their CEOs. Visa (NYSE: V), for instance, is doing well as it rides the growth of ecommerce, with customers often paying with debit and credit cards sporting the Visa logo. The growth of digital payments prompted Visa CEO Alfred Kelly to tell shareholders earlier this year that he wants to move away from debit and credit cards, at least in name, as smartphones, wearables and other devices become increasingly popular payment mechanisms. Technology is allowing Visa to find new ways to leverage its payment network to accelerate its growth. Only time will tell whether Kelly’s preferred term, “payment credentials,” is widely embraced as smartphone-based services such as Apple Pay (NASDAQ: AAPL), wearables such as the Fitbit (NYSE: FIT) and the “Internet of Things” mean more devices will also be used to make payments. Kelly is being richly rewarded for his work at Visa, which paid him more than $20 million last year. Shareholders aren’t likely to complain, given that the shares hit an all-time high of $145.60 today, up almost 28 percent from the start of the year and nearly 93 percent since he became CEO on Dec. 1, 2016. The compensation data comes from a survey prepared for the San Francisco Business Times by executive compensation solutions firm Equilar Inc.
